question: The national debt of the United States is on track to reach \(5 \cdot 10^{13}\) dollars by \(2033.\) How many digits does this number of dollars have when written as a numeral in base \(5?\) (The approximation of \(\log_{10} 5\) as \(0.7\) is sufficient for this problem.)
solution:
A base-\(5\) numeral gains a digit whenever its value reaches the next power of \(5\). Thus a positive integer \(N\) has \(d\) digits exactly when
\[
5^{d-1}\le N<5^d,
\]
or equivalently,
\[
d-1\le\log_5 N<d.
\]
For \(N=5\cdot10^{13}\), change of base gives
\[
\log_5 N
=\frac{\log_{10}5+13}{\log_{10}5}
\approx\frac{13.7}{0.7}
=\frac{137}{7}
\approx19.57.
\]
Using the approximation supplied in the problem, the highest occupied place is \(5^{19}\). The places \(5^{19},5^{18},\ldots,5^0\) total \(\boxed{20}\) digits, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).

solutionMethods.explanation:
Writing every factor of \(10\) as \(2\cdot5\) leaves a small number that we can compare with powers of \(5\):
\[
N=5\cdot10^{13}=2^{13}\cdot5^{14}=8192\cdot5^{14}.
\]
Since
\[
5^5=3125<8192<15625=5^6,
\]
multiplication by \(5^{14}\) gives
\[
5^{19}<N<5^{20}.
\]
A base-\(5\) numeral in this interval starts in the \(5^{19}\) place and ends in the \(5^0\) place. It therefore has \(19+1=\boxed{20}\) digits, choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
solutionMethods.label: Factor out a power of 5
